Have you ever woken up one day and thought "man, I would've loved to experience what it's like living in the Soviet Union"? Well look no further, come to LaoJie Hotpot.

First for some context, we walk in with 9 people to celebrate a birthday, and some people want hotpot and others want BBQ. They say no, you must sit at different tables to make this work. Ok fine, let's do that.

What they don't tell you is, they'll be watching over you like hawks the ENTIRE time you are eating. They'll literally alternate angles to make sure no one is feeding anyone, and they will stop you if try to give even a single bite. Mind you, this is a place where people will regularly leave entire plates of meat behind because they couldn't finish. It will make 0 difference to their bottom line if someone takes a bite of a skewer, yet they're acting like they'll go bankrupt.

Now look, I get it. If you didn't pay for it, don't eat it. So one of our friends buys a separate plate of appetizers because he was interested in trying an item. Then later on, we order the same item (via the all you can eat), they tell each other in Chinese "don't put that in front of that guy, put it on the other side". We only knew this because one of our friends could understand them.

So at this point we're all fed up. We came here to celebrate a birthday and it's been issue after issue. Then comes time to pay the bill, and out of courtesy we still leave a tip (in hindsight $0 would've been the apt amount). But I start crunching the numbers today and guess what I see? They calculated the tip percentage on TOP of the birthday discount AND tax. Meaning when you pay 18-25% as per their suggestion, it's more like you're paying another 5%.

In conclusion, go to one of the million better hotpot places in chinatown.

We enjoyed the fatty beef, beef tongue, pork belly, handmade fish paste, handmade shrimp paste, crab meat stick, and veggies. We each get our own hot pot, so I chose the mushroom soup base. Quality of meat (and others) is much better than other places of similar price range. Service is very prompt. Takes away empty dishes and comes to add to extra items / refill soup often. I see many people get BBQ skewers; they look very good. Place gets crowded, wait can often be 45min to an hour during peak dinner hours. Try to make early reservation if possible.

My all time go-to AYCE hotpot in Manhattan!!   I have been visiting Laojie for almost 10 times over the past 3 years. Their services were top-notch. Super attentive and effective. The food options and quality were amazing, especially for an AYCE grade. They also have a “pay only 3 for 4 party” birthday promo so def check it out.

Great all you can eat hotpot experience. I love the jelly desert at the end! Definitely very convenient location for me. It can get pretty busy, so I would recommend calling them beforehand to ask about availability.

All you can eat hotpot! So yummy and the quality of the food is very good! The fried rice cake dessert at the end of the meal is sooooo good! Also, the jelly dessert at the end is amazing. For only 40 bucks per person (including tax and tip) it is an amazing deal. I would definitely recommend going here if you’re looking for a good hotpot place in Manhattan!

Another great experience at Lao Jie! Started eating at Lao Jie back in 2020 (or whenever it opened) so it's exciting to see the franchise grow into something more! Great and attentive service. Our waiter / waitress were making sure we had water and our soups were refilled every 20-30 minutes. Our (uncooked) food also came out fast. Really affordable considering the amount of food and services we have access to: sauce bar & all you can eat appetizers, meat , seafood, and veggies. The food has never been an issue for me since we (the customers) are cooking them for ourselves. They’re so thoughtfully plated for us to enjoy with our eyes. I've always loved the theme they go for: vintage Chinese films / traditional scenes. This spot did not disappoint the legacy of Lao Jie Hot Pot!
The food was delicious and it was a great experience. It does take them a little while to bring the food to your table but I would still recommend going here!

The ambience of the booths is really nice and it’s great that there is an individual broth pot option.  The fish options were very good. The tomato broth tasted more like sweet ketchup than I’ve had elsewhere.  The lotus root was cut way toot thick to cook and eat in time with other things. Only one member of our group had been before and the staff seemed annoyed when we asked what was and wasn’t included in the ayce. The menu has a lot of unnecessary pages. When it came to paying, the staff brought us the check but didn’t come back for a while so when they came they were aggressive and rushing about paying even though they were the ones who left the table for a long time. The vegetable and mushroom broths are good along with the singing for birthday celebrations but I wouldn’t rush back.
The best all you can eat hot pot in the US!! The service is premium, and the food is so delicious and fresh!!! Strongly recommended!!

Good was very good, and very fresh and fast my served. The only off putting thing was that me and my friend were escorted downstairs to a basement level to dine when there was many open tables upstairs. We noticed all the americans/ non-chinese or mandarin speaking customers were laced downstairs and everyone else were put upstairs in the nice, advertised area. It felt a little weird being seperated by the rest of the restaurant by going to the basement. other then that the staff was very nice and quick, but because of the fact we were placed in the basement makes me not want to return.

Absolutely fantastic hotpot experience at LaoJie Hotpot! The ingredients were fresh, the spicy broth was flavorful, and the ambiance was authentic and inviting. I especially love all the old TV's on the wall. The staff were attentive and made great recommendations. Perfect spot for a fun and delicious meal—will definitely be coming back!
We ordered one serving of beef and they sent us 5. Other than that the food was pretty good
Delicious hot pot and cute place!! Service was great I think quite literally the only thing i would change is leaving a water on the table. Everything else is great this place is wonderful

Came here to celebrate a friend's birthday. They did the whole song and all. The food selections are always consistent here. And we love getting the fried stuff as dessert. Towards the end they missed an order of meat but thats okay.

Vibe/ambiance: clean, casual
Service: standard
Reservation: recommended

Items ordered:
AYCE hotpot - fresh veggies and meat; good soup base options

Grabbed a pudding here to go and it was delicious and jasmine flavored! I think it was jasmine tea and pudding. Cant wait to come back and try more food. Open late relative to other spots in the area.
Service is great food is great come here if you want authentic good hot pot at a fair price

I came here at 10pm on a Sunday.
The host told us that last call to order food was at 10:45, but we would be able to stay until 11:45 when they closed at 12 AM. We had no problem with that and was seated right away.

The servers came over immediately and asked us what we wanted to order for food and we put in a good sized list. The food came so quickly after ordering, except for the meat (beef and pork). We decided to give it some time because this has happened in the past, but by 10:30, we were starting to get full and we wanted to ask the waitress. She said she would ask and walked away. Then a waiter came by at 10:40 explaining last call and asked what we wanted to order and I repeated that we still have not gotten our meat and we might as well order more meat. He uses his headset to try and find out what's happening and I see him come out with trays of meat and he brings them to other tables, including tables that arrived after us and doesn't bring us anything. At this point, a third waitress asked if we want last call and we reiterate to her that we still have not gotten our meat yet other tables had. Finally, the last waitress was able to bring us our meat and even some additional dishes that we didn't order. 

We have had something similar happen in the past where they bring the meat last, maybe because it's the most expensive and they hope we get full off everything else and order less meat? (This is my personal opinion but when it happens more than once, I start to speculate) 

This experience was heightened by the timing of closing but was, regardless, extremely frustrating.

The last waitress was extremely kind and attentive afterwards, to likely diffuse the situation.

solid ayce hotpot place with a decently sized menu. i always end up coming here for a bday which they have deals for. this time i got the clam and winter melon broth but it was pretty flavorless so id get the tomato again next time. compared to a lot of ayce hotpot and kbbq spots i think their beef is actually pretty good quality and i slightly prefer the fatty beef over angus beef. sometimes service can be slow as its usually packed here.

Haven't been to the LaoJie for a while but I don't remember not enjoying my meal at all. Don't get me wrong the service is great but the food was not good. Came by an hour before they close on a Friday night, for the just hot pot AYCE. I ordered the mushroom broth and I didn't like it, it tasted more like msg and you see the mushroom in it. Their beef had a weird taste. The rest of the adds on was okay, but because the meat, it kind of ruin the appetite.
I don't think I will return to this location.
Really regretted coming here. The quality of the meats and the grilled skewers was so bad. Not sure how they got such good ratings all around. Expensive for cheap quality food.

This is the perfect place to satisfy your hot pot craving! It is all you can eat for about $45, and their menu offers a wide range of meats and veggies. As a bonus, they have great dessert items as well. They have a good sauce bar. Service is fast and efficient, and the atmosphere is comfortable. I highly recommend this place if you're in the mood for hot pot!
The hotpot here is so good!! The service was so quick, the waiter was very attentive and kept checking up on us, our water was always full, and the food came quick. When they added broth it was broth

05.17.2026 @7pm
Made reservations for a table of 5 for 6:30pm. Kids was getting here late so waited till 7p to get seated. Our service was consistent accept changing dirty plates. Friendly service throughout. I usually goes to the spot in Brooklyn, glad to tried the manhattan spot. 
The freshness of the quality from any spot of LaoJie hasn't disappoint me so far and LaoJie is still will be one of my favorite hotpot I'll stick with because of the fair price with fair to good freshness of quality!

Good deal $44 for AYCE hotpot bbq (skewers) and sapporo, Can do big table pot or individuals. incl a few appetizers and rice etc. Not as many options as some I've been to, but a good deal. a few premium add ons, and they bring out the bbq not grill yourself. Waiters are very attentive. they bring you some jasmine mango pudding for dessert, no assortment of pastries etc. Overall a good deal for group friends (+bday discount)
Great all you can eat hotpot! Also enjoyed their birthday deal (free on your birthday). I thought the meat quality and the ingredient quality was good!
A good place for all you could eat for personal hot pot in the city. Last time i went for my friends birthday celebration. We really enjoyed it

Thought this was a well priced and well stocked AYCE hotpot. You each get your own pot so if you enjoy the communal aspect of hotpot this will be lacking. Herbal broth was exactly what I needed on a cold day!
I felt physically unwell after eating here, and the staff pressured us into paying a higher tip. This is not how a restaurant should operate. Very disappointing and concerning experience.

Solid AYCE hot pot place for $40pp. Great variety of not only hot pot items but appetizers too (chicken wings, fried buns with condensed milk, pumpkin cakes, etc). Am surprised at this price point with the amount of seafood options as well. At the end, you get a milk tea dessert which my friends really like. 

Seating is spacious but be aware if you're sat towards the back that it is super loud with the music playing. My only complaint would be that the servers kept forgetting our orders and we had to flag them down repeatedly to reorder. 

Also note that there is a two hour time limit and reservations are only held for 10min.

AYCE hot pot, you order from servers who come around to the table, they return platters quite quickly. You have the option of shared broth in a large pot with 2 flavors or individual pots on separate burners. We started off taking visits to the sauce station. Hopefully you know what you like because there are very little instructions or combos that may be nice for anyone who isn't sure where to start. We shared the large pot among 3 of us. Started with gyoza and had fatty beef, pork belly, lamb, sausages, spam, shrimp, rice cakes, thick vermicelli, udon, fish balls, mushrooms, cabbage. At the end a small dessert was served along with the check, there wasn't an option offered or an explanation of what it was. My complaints: I would have loved more options of green vegetables, I prefer either ordering from an iPad or grabbing from a buffet, that other AYCE offer, it's a lot of pressure to quickly decide what you'd like next when the servers walk up. I'd go back, but there are so many more to try!

Yesss please! So good and so much food for just $40ish. The broth was delicious and everything was served almost immediately. We went in toward the end of the night so not too busy. All staff was attentive.

Quality of food is about the price you pay for and they had many options. For our food order, they missed our orders a few times and service was a bit slow. Overall, it was an alright experience as we all left very full at the end of the meal within the time limit.

We paid ~15% tip instead of the suggested 20% for the lack of service. The server asked us to update to the suggested amount because "that is what people normally choose". She stood there for 20 seconds before walking away. After this interaction, I'm not coming back.

Came here with the family for the all you can eat hot pot! Had reservations so we were seated immediately, however the place is kinda small. Servers were pretty attentive and kept coming back from time to time to see if we needed to order any more food. The meats, seafood & veggies were brought raw to the table for us to cook but were all fresh. A good variety of things to choose on the hotpot menu as well. Either way you can't go wrong with hotpot in the winter :)

Very solid spot! What makes this place stand out compared to others is the delicious dessert at the end, it's so good! The non hotpot plates are also quite good, especially the fried buns with condensed milk.

Clean and friendly staff! This is my go to hot pot spot in Chinatown! Honestly there are not much of choices in Chinatown, however it's always been enjoyable coming here. 

One note though, we ordered fish paste instead of shrimp paste because my friend is allergic to seafood. Shrimp paste came anyway, waitress was differentiate if it's shrimp or fish ‍ so please be careful if you have any food allergies.

Laojie Hotpot in Manhattan is one of my absolute go-to spots for high-quality hotpot. From the moment you sit down, you can tell a lot of care goes into both the ingredients and the broths--they're rich, clean, and incredibly well balanced.

My favorite broth is the tomato, which is comforting and slightly tangy, while my close second is the spicy beef tallow soup for when I want something bold and deeply savory. Both are excellent and set the tone for an amazing meal.

When ordering, I always start with fish balls and fish roe balls or the bouncy cuttlefish balls--great texture and full of flavor. From there, move on to fatty beef, but the real standout is the beef tongue. The texture is incredible--tender with just the right bite--and it's a must-order. The tripe and fresh tripe are also favorites of mine: perfectly crunchy without any unpleasant "innards" taste.

Don't skip the fried tofu skin roll--it soaks up the broth beautifully, but pro tip: dip it for only about 20 seconds and take it out so it doesn't turn into a soggy mess. Enoki mushrooms are a crowd favorite and always a must, and adding corn gives a nice pop of sweetness. To really make the most of the broth, add yam noodles, rice cakes, udon, or ramen--you can't go wrong with any of them.

Round out the meal with fresh cabbage, shiitake mushrooms, and watercress for balance and freshness. And save room for dessert--the mango dessert is my favorite way to end the meal and works perfectly as a palate cleanser.

Bonus points for their birthday special, which makes celebrations even more fun. Overall, Laojie Hotpot delivers consistently great food, quality ingredients, and a satisfying hotpot experience every time. Highly recommend.

This AYCE restaurant in Chinatown was bustling on a Sunday night. After asking around it seems like the wait is typically an hour if a reservation was not made in advance. After getting seated, the waitress allowed us to put our clothes in a plastic bag to avoid them getting smelly. The service was very attentive and there is no limit to the dishes you can order each round. There is also an option of half orders, which I really appreciated. The meat was surprisingly good quality too, and not just fatty cuts that other ayce stores provide. At the end of the meal, a milk tea pudding was served, which was sweet and delicious!

Time Went: 6pm on an average Wednesday

Love me some good hotpot, and I've got to say this place doesn't disappoint. There are plenty of choices for dishes, and of all the meats we tried, the Angus beef was definitely our favorite. I went with a group of three, and they allowed us to have two flavors shared, which I went with the healthy herb and the went for their spicy broth (I'm not a big spicy girl). 

There is a table of a bunch of different sauces that you can put together and combine, and I loved this because I like grabbing chopped green onions and chopped garlic to throw into my broth. I also like mixing different sauces together to get a different kind of flavor profile.

The hot pot place is pretty clean and the ventilation is decent. We used LaoJie as a place to surprise our friend for her birthday, and without us telling the staff, by looking at our birthday hats, they played the music around the restaurant to sing happy birthday to her. They also surprised her with a dessert and a gift! 

They have a birthday special here if you bring a certain amount of people (4 I think), the birthday person is free. I'm definitely going to come back for my birthday! 

One Fatal Flaw that almost made me knock this down a Star -- there was no bok choy on the menu at all!!!  Buuuuuut other than that it's pretty solid. Prices weren't bad and they even give you big plastic bags to put your coats in, so they don't smell like hot pot. I didn't realize that so I didn't do it, but I will next time.

I've been such a loyal customer to 99 Favor Taste and Hometown, but my friends and I finally decided to try somewhere new. We came on a Sunday during lunch and were able to be seated right away. I really liked the interior decorations; even the hot pot bowls that they have are cool. They have individual hot pots, and I was surprised to see some pretty unique broth offerings. They have a lot of different options for hot pot ingredients too, and I was impressed by how fresh everything was. We went for the AYCE skewers as well, and they were so many different skewer options too. My only complaint is that some of the skewers were reallyyy overcooked. Like they were more like jerky than grilled meat. But the flavor was good at least!

I loved the free dessert that they gave you. They also had some dessert options that you could order as part of the AYCE menu. Overall, this was a great experience and it might even replace my other normal AYCE hot pot go-tos!

Wonderful food, wonderful service.

I came across this place on complete chance. My friends and I were heading back home from Chinatown and stopped to see if we could use LaoJie's restroom. There were 3 of us and we were unsure if they would even let us in, so we went one by one. Surprisingly, they were kind enough to let us use their restroom and immediately I was stunned by the interior and the smell of their food. I knew I had to come back.

I've gone back 3 times since then and will continue to go and recommend it. Their hotpot is amazing and the servers have always been kind. I took my friend here for her first hotpot experience.

We went here as a big group and the service was really bad. It took around 10 minutes to 15 minutes to call up an order of meat and my group of six (went with 12 people split into two groups) kept eating up all of the meat so quickly because of how little they provide and how much time they make us wait for the food. There was only one server available every 10 minutes for some reason, and it was just a waste of our time because we kept wondering where the food was. Brooklyn location was much more cheaper and the service was significantly better than this location. Complete opposite of the waiting times I had just described for the Manhattan location. It's crazy because it's raw meat getting served and it still took that long to arrive at the Manhattan location and it was just not that worth going here. We did go back to the Brooklyn location, just don't go to the Manhattan one. It's not quick for an AYCE and we never ate our worth (probably at least half because of how slow the service was and we just gave up waiting and left).

This was the most uncomfortable meal I ever had. We came here with a party of 6 for dinner on a Wednesday night. There were plenty of seats and we were able to get a table right away. It was relatively dark in here as the lights were dim. Once we sat down and order the food, I noticed on one of the plate there was a baby roach. I told the staff and they address it very quickly. They gave a new plate, apologized and discounted our bill. Ordered our second plate of meat. As my dad picked it up ready to put the meat in his pot he saw a roach just running around the meat. The staff apologized again and took the plate away. Fast forward a little we saw another roach crawling beside the wall. They staff did offer to switch our table to the one behind but at this point I don't think it made a difference.  Yes I would have left after the second siting of our little friends but because I came with my parents and they gave this place the benefit of the doubt.

Visited LaoJie in Chinatown on a Saturday night and it was surprisingly empty, though we did go close to closing. We arrived around 10:45 p.m. and they closed at midnight. I ordered the bone broth soup, and our group went heavy on the meats since the server told us we had to place all meat orders right away because the kitchen closed at 11. Totally understandable, but it led to us ordering a lot.

The portions here are much larger than most hot pot places, so we definitely over ordered, but we still got everything we needed. The meats such as brisket and pork were fresh and did not seem frozen. All the other items we tried such as meatballs, lobster balls, pork balls, and more were also pretty solid.

I will admit I am not the biggest hot pot fan, but this spot was good and I would come back. Service was fine, nothing out of the ordinary. The space is big and the pricing is decent for New York. Our total came to 190 dollars including tip for four people.

I really wanted to like this place but a few things keep me from coming back. 

First the staff is nice. I made a rsvp over the phone easily and they gave me a bench since I preferred that. Ordering was fast and the food came quickly. They didn't bother explaining anything with what came out l, but I didn't expect that. 

The angus meat was a nice cut. I liked they had the fish roe fish balls. They had a large variety of leafy vegetables, which is nice because 99 favor only has like 2 options. 

The place is a little dirty. There were not many  people there, but our first plate that came out had multiple pieces of hair in it. It was black hair and very obvious. I also saw a spider crawling around the sauce station. 

It is AYCE for only $37 so I guess I can't expect too much but it is just not that clean. So I am not returning.
Hotpot was delicious the was the perfect amount of flavor. The skewers were a bit underwhelming though. It could have had a bit more spice on top. Overall for the price it was decent enough

Our family's favorite AYCE hotpot spot!! The service is always super fast and the staff are all friendly. The food quality is definitely worth the price and meat is fresh. Ambiance inside is good, one of the better decorated hotpot places. We've been here so many times our blood is probably 30% at this point.

This spot surpasses every competitor. Their menu layout made selection easy. Staff is genuinely pleasant and solves all concerns. Great food here doesn't require a big budget. This spot deserves your swift attention.

10/10 Talk about value - AYCE hotpot & skewers, you get so much for what you pay!

We went on a Tuesday evening. $37 for AYCE hotpot or skewers, $43 for both. Although, I think the prices are lower on weekdays because the total bill came out to be $80 after taxes. Very big menu across apps, meats, seafoods, veggies, skewers, & sides.

Spicy beef tallow & tomato broths were both tasty, made everything flavorful. Meats and veggies are all fresh and plated cleanly. Skewers were okay, they all had the same seasoning. There's a sauce station to make your dips too. The dessert which is rice pudding is such a nice way to end too!

Something underrated, they give you plenty of utensils and plates. They gave us a stack of plates, a large cup for disposing skewer sticks & shells, a ladle for broth, slotted ladle to scoop food, and tongs.

Service was very fast and attentive. They are quick-handed tho and they grabbed a couple of things that were half eaten so be sure to let them know if you want to keep something haha. 

Vibe is fun! They play some good Chinese music, I shazam'd a few times. The decor is fiery and woody.

Overall this was amazing - great bang for your buck. Definitely coming back.

Probably my all time favorite hot pot place. Service is fast. Staff friendly and efficient. They give you all the pot, tongs, strainer utensils. Broths are always well seasoned and the food overall gives the vibe of a nice home cooked meal. Wait times are either non-existent or not to bad I've found. And the all day AYCE is unbeatable.

we left a phone on the table and they pawned it off to some old guy on the street ;(

we asked for the phone multiple times and they insisted it wasn't there, meanwhile, they had given it to some random guy to walk off and make a profit off of it. very sad because the food was good.

don't trust this place. pathetic...

LaoJie has a great vibe and a decent price for their AYCE hotpot. There is a small room in the back too where it looks like you can fit a small party for a celebration. The meats were decent quality and they had a great selection - the lamb was my favorite. Overall a solid option for hot pot in Chinatown!

I'm a fan of hot pot and this place meet my expectations. The quality of the meat is really good, the servers are very nice and attentive. There are so many variety of meat cut that you wouldn't get at other places, some of seafoods are fresh (make sure you get the shrimp paste). The spicy soup was flavorful (I would avoid the pork bone soup). The appetizers and desserts options are okay.

I've been going to the original 8th ave location since it opened in 2018, and it continues to be my favourite AYCE (all you can eat) hot pot spot across the city. The workers go out of their way to make your party feel welcome and accommodate different types of eaters (no pork, included). The portions are always super fresh and well presented, assuring you that they put the utmost care into the customer. There's usually old school Chinese/HK pop playing on the screens in the background which are routinely interrupted by their iconic "Happy Birthday" choruses, since you can eat free +/-1 day within your birthday. The sauce bar is also self-serve and stellar.

The only reason I'm giving this location a 4 and not a 5 is because they charge more (~5/10$) and the quality was JUST slightly lesser quality, though still better than Hometown BBQ nearby (which is also superb).

I came here for a dinner with friends the day before my birthday and was pleasantly surprised to find out that they give you free AYCE if it's within 3 days of your birthday! The interior of the restaurant is a bit more traditional and cozy with lots of booths for hot pots. You order with staff here and their service is fairly quick.

You have the option to do individual hotpot or communal hotpot and my friends and I opted for the communal hotpot. We ordered a variety of meat, veggies, and other ingredients and everything was delicious. The veggies were fairly fresh and the meats were good quality for AYCE, and there were so many options to choose from. For the value, I think this is a great deal. And, at the end of the meal you can get free dessert (a pudding), AND if it's your birthday then you can get shaved ice and a free chopstick set!

Delicious broth, great selection of sauces, and a well-stocked menu. We enjoyed the fish balls with roe, the thinly sliced beef and pork, the ginormous clams, and just the interior vibe. It was a bit too loud for us but otherwise we had a good time!

Another great experience at Lao Jie! Started eating at Lao Jie back in 2020 (or whenever it opened) so it's exciting to see the franchise grow into something more! Great and attentive service. Our waiter / waitress were making sure we had water and our soups were refilled every 20-30 minutes. Our (uncooked) food also came out fast. Really affordable considering the amount of food and services we have access to: sauce bar & unlimited meat , seafood, and veggies. The food has never been an issue for me since we (the customers) are cooking them for ourselves. They're so thoughtfully plated for us to enjoy with our eyes. I've always loved the theme they go for: vintage Chinese films / traditional scenes. This spot did not disappoint the legacy of Lao Jie Hot Pot!

Came here on a cold weekend night, perfect for hot pot. The wait was about 1 hr, had plenty of time to explore and checkout Manhattan Chinatown and to empty some space for the all you can eat. So we ordered the all you can eat and we ordered multiple proteins, veggies, and fried buns. They were all fresh, delicious, and came out pretty quickly. I'd say the fatty beef was the most enjoyable and worth dish to order. All other proteins were good as well. I'd say this the meal was very worth it and the price is well deserved it considering it was all you can eat. Will definitely come back to this place again in the future for all you can eat as well : )

This is my favorite hot spot in the city (of the one's I've tried)! The wait is never longer than 20 minutes in my experience and they have a lot of variety of food to order from including fried food for AYCE hot pot!

Top items: 
- Bone cylinder soup base (rich and warm, perfect soup base for me since it's not spicy) 
- Fish balls with fish roe (must get always!! So happy they have this) 
- Fatty beef
- Fish fillet 
- Shrimp paste (essentially ground up shrimp and when cooked turns into a meatball kind of texture) 

Everything comes out so quickly and the portions are fairly small so you can order a good amount of items without feeling like you are going overboard. They also have a sauce bar which is included in the AYCE price! This is also a great place to go if you have a big group, I saw multiple tables seated for 6.

Definitely one of the better AYCE hotpot places around NYC & worth - they also offer AYCE BBQ skewers! 

We came in right as they opened so we were seated immediately. My party of 3 chose both the AYCE hotpot + skewer options. They have a huge variety of hotpot items including my favorite - beef tongue! My friend was pleasantly surprised that they served AYCE osmanthus intestines (桂花腸) because it was one of her favorites and not a lot of places even offer it. The soup bases are all pretty delicious. The milk tea pudding dessert that they serve at the end always yummy!

Food quality is good & it came out pretty fast. The staff was really attentive as well.

wasn't sure if it was an off-day for the waiter but the service was a bit horrible for us. 

We had a group of 6 and waited 10ish mins for our table on a Saturday evening.  The waiter was in a foul mood or something was just rolling his eyes every time we wanted something; it got to the point where we tracked another waiter down instead. Even though this is an AYCE, we ordered alcohol.. guess that was too much work for him.!

Why is this place so popular ? I mean its nice that its AYCE and like $45 per person but what in the actual ...? The meat is super low quality. Stringy, fatty, yucky cheap cheap. There is very few choices for meat. I really liked the beef tongue but thats about it. Their tenderized meat straight up tasted rotten. DO NOT GET. I immediately threw up after putting it in my mouth. The smell, the rancid taste? all of it. I will never come here again.

A new favorite of mine when it comes to hot pot. From ingredients to offerings to customer service, Lao Jie is my go to place for a warm hungry meal. The selection is expansive with ingredients that other all you can eat restaurants don't typically offer. Not only that their seafood (crab and large clams) is very fresh and appetizing as well as their wide selection of 6+ soup bases. At the end of it, they provider a unique jasmine yellow pudding that is "not too sweet" (code for just right sweetness). I would buy that as dessert to go. 

During dinner time, especially weekends they do get busy and so if you have reservations they start you immediately. Otherwise, the service and staff members are welcoming and attentive.

This is my favorite AYCE spot! For the value alone, it's worth coming. The broths are flavorful, service is excellent, and the ambiance transports you to China. The quality of the food is really good and they also offer some already cooked dishes. Can't forget about their complimentary dessert which is a milk tea pudding, so good! Highly recommend!

I may be biased because I absolutely love hot pot with a passion. AYCE hot pot less than $40? Say less!! There were so many options, the quality was great, free sauces and dessert. We waited for 45 min on a Saturday night when we were quoted 1.5 hours. It's very vibey and lively in there. This is definitely going to be my go to hot pot spot. I am still dreaming of the food.

To-go spot for AYCE hotpot beside Hometown Hotpot a few blocks away. I've always made a reservation before coming here to avoid long wait times. The food here is great and they have many options for hotpot. I love the large variety they offer for all the meats and veggies. Also, if you go on your birthday it's discounted!! 

Side note: they provide a large bag for you to put your jackets in so they don't soak up the hotpot smell.

Bring your friends here for their birthday! Good bang for your buck AND you get "Happy Birthday" blasted for you AND they give you a goodie bag AND bday person eats for free

Quality is definitely not high but you get what you pay for here. Still, lots of great options on the menu to choose from! A good casual spot to just have a good time with friends

As the year is coming to an end, my friend and I decided to wrap up 2024 with a bang...at none other than LaoJie Hot Pot (老街火锅吧) for AYCE hot pot in Lower East Side, Chinatown. We'd made a reservation for 4:30pm few days ago and saw that hardly anyone was there because it wasn't after work hours yet upon arrival. Huge plus that the reservation for a party of two is allowed w/o needing at least 4+ people in the group compared to other hot pot spots.

Got greeted by the staff as we walked in right away. The Manhattan location is just like the Brooklyn locations (upstairs & downstairs) - very decently sized with retro-styled booths for larger parties and tables of four to fit smaller groups of 2-4 people.

Chinatown Laojie Hot Pot is hands-down one of the best spots for hot pot in the area. People gathering to mix their own sauces in the self-serve sauce bar + the delicious aroma of simmering broths + a lively, welcoming vibe. The restaurant is clean and well-organized, which made the experience even better.

LJHP's retro-style decorations are a feast for the eyes, welcoming diners to a mix of rich Chinese history down the memory lane. The vintage posters, cassette tapes, traditional red lanterns, dim lighting, and rustic wooden furniture help to create a cozy & authentic setting. Every corner is thoughtfully designed, making it as the perfect photo opps. Customers can really feel the charm of classic Chinese culture throughout the space. It's not just a meal--more like an experience!

The menu is decently large, offering some of its fresh ingredients to cook in your choice of broth. My friend and I both chose the herbal soup base--as it had just the right amount of flavor w/o too much MSG. The angus beef and lamb slices were super fresh and the texture melted on our tongue; the vegetable (spinach + A-lettuce) options were pretty fresh as well.

Overall, pretty good food + flavorful & not too salty broth. The highlight of the whole experience was definitely the free house-made fragrant mango milk tea pudding at the end for dessert. I wish they would sell that from the menu. Could eat at least a few bowls after hot pot.

Service was quick and friendly, staff had checked in on us very often to refill broths in the pot and our water cups. Prices are reasonable even for dinner time considering the quality and portion sizes. They accept both cash/credit card now. If you're a hot pot lover, this place is a must-try!

Good thing that we went there earlier--didn't get crowded until around 6pm when others started coming as we got ready to leave. There was even a party of 7 sitting in the front by the doorway at the waiting area.

The Downsides + Improvements could be made:

1) Staff had forgotten some of our food options twice (only gave 2 pieces of sausages & no fried tofu skins) throughout the meal despite not being dinner rush hours.

2) Only two napkins were brought to our table, I'd to get up & search for a stack of napkins myself by the sauce bar.

3) Staff hadn't offered a plastic bag to put our jackets in to prevent from smelling like hot pot when we sat down at the table. Didn't know we could've asked the staff either beforehand until reading other Yelpers' reviews.

Thank you for reading!  
That's it for now....

(Overall: A) - I greatly enjoyed this AYCE Hotpot place for under $50/pp. Before the meal started, the staff already made a great impression by providing a large plastic bag to wrap our jackets, which solved a longstanding mystery of how I can get rid of the hotpot/kbbq smell from my clothes. Their menu has an impressive array of choices to choose from, ranging from your classic cuts of proteins and cuts to some more adventurous such as aorta and tripe, loved by those born with this taste. There is a healthy array of vegetables and carbs, as well as a good selection of sweets and appetizers to round out the meal, which can be ordered by piece -- I really enjoyed the fried pumpkin. LaoJie was quite spacious and all of the food was presented nicely and seemed reasonably fresh. Good quality hotpot overall!

Food: +1
Presentation: +1
Price: E
Atmosphere: +1
Service: +1 
Menu: +1
Overall: +5 A

Insta/Beli/TikTok: @amei_eats
Perfect spot to meet your friends and eat quality food in a very energetic space! Don't wear your special clothes as you will come out covered in the aroma! Definitely a must stop while in the area!

For $37 a person, all you can eat meats and veggies is a good deal in New York. The food is fresh enough for buffet style and the service is very quick and attentive. Drinks not included but everyone in my party was full and satisfied. I like the angus beef here, which not all hot pots in chinatown offer, and the selection of veggies to convince myself I am healthy.

Bonus is a 5% discount paying with cash or a free drink for each person. We took the cash discount, and we will be back again
DELICIOUS FOR A GOOD PRICE!! The quality is so good, it's worth the price! I love a good AYCE spot Service was good, the server was really attentive! Casual spot, but cute decor :) Would come back

The all you can eat hot pot was very good. Meats were very nice. There was a decent selection of veggies. There were lots of seafood options. The watermelon juice was amazingly smooth and to tasty. I would highly recommend adding that on. The service was top notch. It seemed to be mostly birthday celebrations other than us so there was a lot of happy birthday singing by the staff and the music was entirely too loud. Other than that it was amazing though. 10/10 would go again.

Great fun dinner on a chilly day! Came here for my birthday and they offer a free meal which is nice.  I liked it's all you can eat and got to try the different fresh meats and vegetables in mushroom broth.  Also got watermelon juice which was refreshing but the best was the dessert, it was a light pudding and had some tea infused in it, was so tasty!   Service was good but they did forgot the vegetables in the beginning.  They also sing happy birthday but I opted out since they sang it about 5 times before me, and they give a gift but had to ask for it.
Favorite AYCE hot pot! Great price, value, and quality of ingredients! Huge variety of meats and veggies, really fresh, and great sauce bar!

great place to try with a big group. had individual pots so we could all get our own broth. the servers were patient and attentive and explained the menu to us. the hotpot and skewer combo was a great deal and had a nice variety of seafood items. Meat plates were very good portion and high quality. the fried buns and pumpkin pancake were so good, as well as the dessert pudding. would return for AYCE

The food and the waiter/waitress services are alright; similar to other Chinese restaurants. However, the reason I gave this restaurant a lower star is the attitude of the manager/ owner at the receptionist desk in the front. When my group of 4 arrived last late night, he forgot to put our group name or phone number down. We were sitting across him the whole time. After seeing a couple of other parties arrived after us but were able to get their tables ahead of us, we reminded him and he put our phone number down; but still let others went ahead. He knew we waited there but still purposely let others (same party size walk in) ahead of us. I wanted to walk out at that moment but some of my friends were too tired to change to a new restaurant, and many nearby restaurants were closed, so we stayed and got a table after a very long wait.

Staff were so kind and accommodated me even though it was late and they were about to close the kitchen. Made sure to come by frequently in the 20 minutes before the kitchen closed so I still had an opportunity to order everything I wanted. Definitely felt I got my moneys worth. Phenomenal service and even though it was late on a Monday night they were all smiles. Interior was very nicely decorated, I enjoyed the music and atmosphere. They even left me a little desert at the end. Left full and happy. Would definitely recommend if you are a fan of great service and food.

I visited 12/2/24. If you are the owner and reading please know your staff are killing it from open to close! Very impressed. Looking forward to visiting again.

Hotpot at its best. This is one of my favorites. It is a spacious location with two levels of seating. Made reservations as I was visiting with friends, and heard that it does get pretty packed. Reservations of 4 were. honored over the phone. The hostess spoke a mixture of Mandarin + English. My party was seated promptly in the upstairs dining area. Menus are extensive with an option for hotpot + bbq or just one or the other. We all opted for hotpot. Bags are given to hold your jackets if needed. 3/4 of us ordered the tomato broth, and 1 ordered the herbal. There are other varieties as well. Tomato has a good balance, infused with scallion and ginger but not overly strong. Proceeded to order a bunch of meats ranging from beef and pork belly to various seafoods and vegetables. There are also cooked foods made to order that come with the food. We opted for fried bread, French fries, dumplings and meat. Raw items include beef, pork belly,  veggies, mushrooms, egg, to name a few. The menu is so extensive including seafoods and other items that can be ordered a la carte. Service was prompt and didn't need any addressing. There is a sauce bar close to the front that you can mix and match different sauces and garnish to your liking. Really enjoyed dinner and can't complain because there was so much food , and I left so full. You are given 90 minutes to eat and are told that upfront. Will be back to try other items on the menu and mix it up with different broths and sauces.

The worst experience I ever had!!
1) When we first come in, we just sit down, we didn't even open the menu, the lady come and ask "you guys ready to order", we was like let us take a look first, then she said "the 2 hours limit starts count". So which mean you no matter what, first you sit down the 2 hours all you can eat time will starts count!!!
2) So we rush to order since she push us so much, then we order foods for 4 ppls, then the foods came, the table already FULL, and the waiter brought another 6-8 plates of meat, so I saw the next table who had only 1 ppl sit there with one extra small table that can help to put dishes. I asked them can we have one since the table already no space for the 6-8 plates of meat, they refused it. I was like I need to speak to your manager, the lady was like oh she need to speak to manager wor!!!!. So finally they give us the small table to put the extra foods. 
3) this is not Laojie I knew, cause we went to the one on Brooklyn so many times, we love their service and foods. BUT the one in Chinatown, even you gave me for free I will never come again!!!

Forever my favorite hot pot restaurant in NY. For $36.98pp, you get AYCE hot pot with a huge variety of protein, veggies, seafood, noodles, and more. 

The service is also quick as everything is brought out soon after we ordered. Everyone gets individual hot pots, so you can choose whatever soup base you like. I usually enjoy the tomato, but ventured off with the dark chicken this time which was soothing. There's lot of great seafood options like crab, clams, and mussels to make your money's worth. We also ordered some drinks along with our dinner, which were tasty. 

At the end of the meal comes the best part --the rose milk tea pudding! Seriously one of the best desserts I've ever had and I always look forward to this here. Come for your birthday and you get to eat free with 3 paid guests too.

A surprise hit for me as this is now probably one of my favorite spots in the city for AYCE Chinese hotpot! While ideally it'd be more efficient to order off a device, tracking the servers down to add more meat was still quite fast and the meat quality was good enough for AYCE.

Winter is amongst us so you know what that means.. Hotpot time!!!

Was in between this and Hometown. So happy we decided to go with LaoJie. 

Had the herbal broth. It was very rich in flavor. AYCE spot. All the items we ordered was fresh. They refill your broth frequently. Service was friendly.

Left with a full belly.

Food 4.0/5.0
Service 3.5/5.0
Value 4.0/5.0
Decor 3.5/5.0
Overall 4.0/5.0

Decent AYCE hotpot/skewer chain. Prices are very reasonable and quality is okay. You largely get what you pay for with hot pot but fair to say this spot is on the efficient frontier.

This place HIT the spot. Yagurl was craving good asian food after being in europe. And earlier in the day, I had a very disappointing pad see ew so I was in dire need of my asian food fix. I came here after dance rehearsal and was ready to grub. Everything was so tasty! From the broth, meats, veggies and sauces. Decently priced too. It's also funny that they gave me the family sized pot instead of a small one. I bet people thought this skinny girl must've been a competitive eater!

Went here 7:45pm on a Saturday night and had a wait for 2 people for an hour. 

It's AYCE. You get to choose between communal or individual broth. I had the mushroom brother and my boyfriend had the spicy broth. Their sauce bar is standard. Restrooms are clean. Ingredients are fresh and they were quick to refill broth. They also had a milk tea flavored dessert that was nice to wrap things up.

Great AYCE hotpot for $37 pre tax/tip! You get 2 hours here and that's enough time to overeat. Service was fast and our waiter didn't blink at the looong list of items we ordered over multiple rounds. Pretty comprehensive menu of meat/veg/seafood/noodles/etc and ingredients all looked fresh. The atmosphere was much nicer than other hotpot restaurants I've been to; there are red lanterns along the side and neat faux flames stretching across the main room. Note there are two floors, and we ended up in the basement which isn't bad, but ask to be seated on the main floor if possible. Do make a reservation in advance because the place was full (Friday evening).

Our group of 4 split a tomato and bone broth pot and especially liked the shrimp paste, all the beef cuts, rice cakes, tong hao, napa cabbage, enoki mushrooms, and glass noodles. One of the highlights for me is the dessert that's included - a mango jasmine milk tea pudding that wasn't overly sweet and tasted amazing.

Looking to make another visit here and recommend to anyone looking for good hotpot in the city!

everything was pretty delicious! 

for my broth I got wintermelon and clam! it was my first time seeing a broth for hotpot like that and I was so overjoyed bc I love both wintermelon and clam :) we ordered a bunch of diff meats, Napa cabbage, enoki mushrooms, and fried bean curd! we also got fried mantou with condensed milk (not pictured) it's literally my favorite thing ever~ and they gave us a free shaved ice to share at the end + egg pudding (not pictured) 

service is pretty good! they refill your broth multiple times and come by for more orders. 

interior is sort of rustic. it's nice inside and not too loud. I was able to easily have a conversation with my table! and i was able to witness a birthday celebration (they go all out for that)

Overall Laojie is my one of fav all you can eat hot pot. They carry a lot variety of food, drink, and desserts. 

I love the fried bun, fries, lamp, meat balls etc. I always get their tomato soup base , it's very refreshing and tasty. I can't handle spicy. If you love spicy, try their spicy hot pot.  

Staff is friendly. 

Waiting time can be up to two hours. Last time I waited an hour n I simply put my name and phone number to the staff. The staff called me when it's my turn. So I don't have to wait. Great experience

my favorite ayce hotpot spot in ny!! it does get super busy around dinner so try calling ahead for a reso!

restaurant has a "warm" & cozy feel, the servers are attentive & food always comes out fast! i love the bone broth, pork belly, brown sugar rice cakes, and the mango dessert at the end :)

My favorite hotpot spot in the city! The ambiance is really cool and fun, and the bone broth option is my absolute favorite. Sauce station has great options and is always clean. Quality of food is always great every time I go. Service was accommodating, getting us a table as quickly as possible.

This place always hits! Never a bad meal here.

The seafood, beef and veggies always taste good and sauce bar has it all.

Can't forget the dessert pudding here. So good!!!

Veges and meats are fresh. Soup bases are delicious. The ginger, red dates, and goji berries in the chicken soup reminded me of my childhood. I don't like a heavy, salty soup base. This was just right for me. It might be a little bland for others. The tomato soup is tastier.
Service is attentive. Our server came over to take our orders as soon as we opened the menu. They refilled our ice water and soups many times throughout the night.  Food came out quickly.
The music was too loud. We had to yell across the table to chat with each other, which took away from the communal experience. Could turn the music down a few notches.
Overall, it's a solid ayce hotpot place.

Lao Jie is one of my favorite hot pots in the city.  For the price you get unlimited meat and veggies which is well worth it especially with a big group.  Everything comes out so fast and the food is delicious.  The spicy broth is really spicy but so flavorful and the tomato broth is pleasantly sweet.  Don't expect a lot of pleasantries when it comes to the staff but the food makes up for it.  There is a sauce bar with all of the typical options and they offer a free jasmine tea pudding with dessert which is fruity and refreshing.   I have visited now many times and will continue to be a loyal patron.

Great AYCE hot pot in Manhattan. As a 99 favors loyalist I'm won over. The vegetable quality is great and the meat quality is great. Fine sauce bar too. I haven't tried to skewers. 

Service is great, they're attentive and nice for a Chinese hot pot place. 

It looks really great inside and is a fun spot to take people, but the music is a little loud and whack, and would be super super super great if the AC was just colder.

This is hands down my favorite hot pot chain. They have the best quality ingredients, service, and selection. I enjoy all the soup bases, free fried appetizers, and desserts. I have been to this location over 7 times and I still love it here. This is exactly the spot I would recommend to everyone that wants hot pot.

Rude waitress today who rolled her eyes all night. She had an attitude when seating us and threw the check down on the table at the end. Idk what her problem was, but someone like that should not be customer facing. Send her to the basement or back to the coven she came from

Also don't let them seat u in the basement. It smells so bad (no air ventilation) and looks like a storage room, which I'm sure it was before they put a couple tables and chairs in it and started calling it "seating". This is not the way to expand the space

Laojie Hotpot in Manhattan is serving up an unbeatable deal for all you can eat hotpot lovers! For just $37 you can indulge in their AYCE hotpot, and for only $44 enjoy both hotpot and delicious skewers BBQ! 

With a vast menu of fresh ingredients and mouthwatering BBQ delights, you'll never run out of options. They also got a great selection of broths to choose from! Plus , their interiors are super cool.

Don't miss out on this amazing experience while you're in Chinatown, Manhattan. Head over to Lao jie hotpot and treat yourself! 

Follow @spinx17 for more NYC food adventures!

A great place for all-you-can-eat hotpot and BBQ! I went there with my friends for a quick dinner while we were in Manhattan. It was Sunday night, and we got in right away. Everything was fresh, with many selections of meats and veggies.

The interior had cute traditional Chinese decor, creating a cozy atmosphere. The service was great and very accommodating.

At the end, they offer a free milk tea pudding dessert, which was surprisingly good. It was refreshing, not too sweet, and we loved it so much. My friend even ate two bowls by herself! Lol. They also sell them. Highly recommend this place for those who love hotpot!

I used to come here a lot for either birthday parties or just for dinner. Recently coming here, I noticed that they were no longer doing free birthday dinners, only 50% off. To be honest, it doesn't even make a difference as you are basically paying  for your meal through the tip. 

On Friday night, I dined out with friends at Laojie. I noticed that they had changed the menu and prices have increased by a dollar or two. They were very quick to bring out the food and the waiter were always ready to take our order when we were looking at the menu. We noticed a piece of hair after putting the food into the hotpot and called the waiter over. They apologized and we thought nothing of it. 

When our two hours were up, they bought us the jelly desserts and 10 minutes later they bought the check to our table. As they saw that we weren't leaving they had the manager come over to tell us to leave but we were still in the midst of finishing our food. We haven't ordered anything 30 minutes before our time was up. 

We quickly finished up our food and left. Although service was quick in bringing food, I felt that the waiters provided less table service as we used to have waiters that would help us get rid of the fatty oil in the soup base and etc. 

I feel like I would not be coming back anymore especially how pricey it has become as we paid $100 in total for 2 people without even ordering drinks.

Food, service, ambience, all amazing. 10/10!! The workers are so kind and attentive, my gf was able to charge her phone. Music is suchhh a vibe, they were playing #throwbacks!! Hotpot is firee + the appetizer skewers are insane. Go get the pork belly + inoki mushroom skewer. We are literally still here and I'm writing this review because it's so damn good. I love you LaoJie
This is the other ayce hot pot/ skewers place around here I would recommend. It taste better than the other ones around like hometown. Service is good and the decoration is interesting.

If you're a fan of hotpot, you absolutely need to check out this place! It's all you can eat for hotpot, barbecue, or both together. The beef tongue is a standout - tender, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. Not a lot of places in Chinatown offer beef tongue as an option. The broth is rich and savory, my favorite is their classic bone broth or the dark chicken ginseng The decor is very traditional Chinese with a modern yet cozy ambiance. The service is also great; people are nice and food comes out fast. At the end you also get a free jasmine milk tea pudding dessert. Highly recommend!

I've come here twice, both times for a birthday. The quality of the food was pretty solid-everything was fresh and tasty. I got the herbal soup base one time and the tomato one the other time, but I preferred the tomato soup base-it had strong tomato flavor and was delicious. I liked the angus beef, fatty beef, and the shrimp paste the best. The skewers are also really good-they are all very flavorful. I especially liked the bacon wrapped enoki and the beef ones. Also love the retro decor/aesthetics of the restaurant.

Servers were friendly and quick to come to our table. Whenever I picked up a menu, it seemed like there would immediately be a server beside the table ready to take my next order. They also came and sang happy birthday and gave us free fried buns to celebrate. The only thing is that the first time I went, they forgot to bring out some of the stuff that we had ordered and we had to re-order those things when we realized it never came. 

They also have a nice milk tea jelly dessert at the end that was tasty.

Food selection was very good. Standouts were blue crab, stuffed fishballs, thick vermicelli, and the wagyu beef. We tried everything. Servers were all very friendly and nice. Sauce station was kept clean. Floors are a little sticky, but they had mats out. Nice that we got a free birthday meal, bring ID for proof and they'll sing you a song. I would go back again and I'm not a big hot pot fan. Ended the meal with a free dessert that we enjoyed.

Laojie is one of those aesthetically themed restaurants, with lots of references to a more traditional Chinese vibe. The decor is pretty cool, and they have tables with both individual and table cooking spots. The AYCE for hotpot only is about $37pp ($45 w tip), which is reasonable for Manhattan prices. There's a 2 hour time limit that they keep track of.

Pros:
- Meat was pretty nice quality, not brought up frozen!
- Their milk tea pudding was so good. We all had like 2 bowls!
- Sauce bar, options for food were good
- Broth was decent flavor wise
- They take reservations pretty easily
- Service was good about topping off our waters/broth quickly

Cons:
- The service was pretty off putting. They were really really strict about certain things, but hard to call over in other cases. We had a party of 10, and they would let us only do a max of 2 people not doing AYCE. For the people not doing AYCE, they'd watch super closely and threaten to charge if they saw them eating a piece of meat.
- They didn't bring out any veggies until like 45 into the dinner, so it was a bit slow

They charge their tip total on after tax and not pre-tax. Also the server chased us out with the wrong receipt as we had an adjustment with a 5% discount but he came out with the right without it and asked us to pay the total on the wrong amount plus more on the tax as well. Never coming back. Everyone be careful on your total bill.

Good value per person and quality of hot pot food was very good and fresh. Atmosphere was nice, basement had no phone signal but they had wifi. The server was very attentive. Would definitely go again!

I usually come here for the hotpot, the food was good, but the service was horrible! Extremely disappointed with how we were treated. The blonde hair girl host was extremely rude, didn't even bother to greet us and gave us so much attitude when we were trying to get seated. The second girl threw the menu on the table and didn't even bother to acknowledge us or say anything. They need to train their employees better, this is not how they're suppose to treat customers.

Since service is back to normal compared to the first time that I came, of course, they earned more stars in my book.  

The food is good as always and the staff is nice and friendly.
Great place!! Quality is good and they have so many options. It's a good AYCE price and they even let you dine for free on your birthday. Overall, 10/10 :)
Been here many times and still will visit again. The service is great. They are so attentive. The food is great and the price is worth it. The restaurant is clean. A lot of choices to choose from.

this spot offers all you can eat. love the interior and its spacious. each person can get their own individual pot. service is quick once you order. if you dine on your birthday with at least a party of 4, the birthday person gets their meal free.
Service was really good, food as well, space was not as big, but was nice and cozy, everything was nice and clean too

Food, service, ambiance, fresh meat, delicious soup based! Highly recommended this place. And make sure you make reservation or else your wait will be more than 30 min, sometimes can be 1.5-2 hours long wait...

Ehh was pretty mid. Service was okay. They will bring stuff right away. Soup base was just okay. We got the herbal and spicy. I think ambiance on first floor was better but we got pushed to basement.  Not worth it for that price if you are sitting in basement without ambiance. The fan blows on you and you smell like hotpot after there. Cell Service is spotty so if you are expecting calls...just a warning/heads up

We did ask about upstairs but they said it was a 30 minute wait though I saw a lot of empty tables available. Maybe those were reserved. Who knows. 


I prefer hometown more even though that one is not AYCE.

Honestly, so surprised to find an ayce place that will provide so much food! Where I came from they only gave us a little bit at once, but here nope a bunch at once! A lot variety of meat, veggies, and seafood! I definitely will come back again! The service was great too, didn't bother us too much but provided refills and added soups. I recommend make a reservation or come here early! It's a big restaurant but, it fills up quickly. Love the decoration theme here too! Overall, enjoyed my time and definitely will want to come back again and the again

Some of the best hotpot I've had in the city. Huge quantities, great options, and the ambiance is nice with everyone singing happy birthday often. No reservations so be prepared to wait for a table, especially on the weekends/during the evenings.

Always love hotpot. Lao Jie is always great. We usually eat at the one in Brooklyn but we were in the city and wanted to try it out. They have more options on the menu as opposed to the Brooklyn locations. I always go for the shrimp paste that's my favorite. The service is very good and helpful. If you plan on going there is a discount with cash but they do accept credit card. When we went it was lunch on a weekday so there weren't many people. Very clean and very quiet. You wouldn't think that you were eating in the city.

Tasty AYCE hotpot, I liked the place because you can try three different flavors of soup. It's very loud though, they sang happy birthday like three times while we were there. I was very full afterwards, there's a large selection of meat and vegetables and I wasn't missing anything. They also give you these milk buns while you eat, and milk tea pudding at the end as free dessert which was sooo good. We also got the watermelon slush drink which was refreshing. It's pretty expensive though, was about $45 per person.

food 10/10
service 10/10
ambiance 10/10
I was here couple weeks ago and it was a great experience. 
My server was really nice, he explained everything and gave us some recommendations. he also gave us some milk tea pudding at the end which was delicious. 
definitely come back !

I've been twice to this location already and it's definitely impressing me more than 99 Favors haha. 

After you place your order, everything comes out pretty fast, even despite the insane dinner rush time dining hours. They did miss some items, but no worries, we just ordered them again. We were ordering five plates of fatty beef at a time, multiple rounds, (we had a big group!) and they didn't even blink an eye ahah. Had a great time, the quality of the food is pretty good too. I ordered crab and there was so much roe and they weren't skimping out per order either!

5 - Exceeded expectations
Great pricing for AYCE Hot Pot. Lots of options, and service is very fast. Would recommend.

Got the private room as we do for many many birthdays. The minimum charge for a room is $288 and the time of this post per person is $32. They have two tables in the room. One with 6 hotpot's and one with 4. There's also karaoke. Food is usual hot pot staples with crab shrimp and clams. Everything was fresh and yes we will be back.

Lao jie is one of the best skewer / hotpot restaurants in lower Manhattan - it's hard NOT to recommend to anyone craving that skewer / hotpot combo in an AYCE style. 
Outside of its retro-grade aesthetics, I need to point out that when I went, Lao Jie's service was top-tier ! Waiters and waitresses were extremely attentive, always refilled water, and food came out relatively quickly. 
Fish tofu skewers were really additive, couldn't get enough of it! 
Overall, had a great time and I think the selection of food justifies the price. 
At the end of your meal, you can ask for as many amounts of "milk pudding", which was such a great way to end our dinner.

They made us wait for a long time and let others behind us go I think they forgot about us and then when my friend asked again they had a table for us. The food was good but unlike other hotpot places I've been to, the hotpot smell sticks onto your hair and clothes for days despite washing several times to try and get rid of the smell

One of my favorite places to go with a large friend group. I've been here at least three times. I love the split bowl options. They have the option for individual, but split bowls are better for bonding in my opinion! My personal favorites are the spicy broth, tofu skins, fish balls, and any beef. the service is always good. There is an ATM if you forget or don't have enough cash.

Ambiance (5/5): There was plenty of seating on a random weekday lunch hour. I love-love-loved the interior design; it feels both like inside a jungle with a fake fire divider in the middle, retro TVs along the way, and a back private room with real windows between the walls. Lao Jie means old town hence the décor of the traditionally dressed women on the wall artwork, retro cassette tapes, sewing machine, etc. 
Service (5/5): They took our jackets and sealed them up in a plastic garbage bag under the table to avoid stinking it up. I also really appreciated the staff uniform of the red handkerchiefs and striped shirts, which strangely reminded me of a French person. I liked how the menu had photos and we placed the orders with the staff. They were quick to bring out and clear our used dishes.
Food:
AYCE hotpot + BBQ skewers ($44): Definitely opt solely for their AYCE hotpot--the bbq skewers were just ok and half of the meat we got was either too tough or not great. The broth was good and plenty of flavors to try at the sauce station. Their house sauce was great! At the end, we were given a free dessert of some kind of jelly pudding that sweet and tasty.  
It may not be the best hotpot I've had but for the cost and great service, I would recommend to friends!

I have always heard from friends that Laojie Hot Pot is good. I happened to be shopping and passed by Chinatown so I stopped by to try it. The result was quite disappointing. The dishes I ordered were not all available. The final tip was 15% before tax. , but before leaving, a waiter asked for a tip and said it was not enough. It turned out that he was asking for their recommended tip after tax. I will not go there again. It is illegal to ask for an after-tax tip. Don't you understand?

Do NOT go here.  Possibly the worst dining experience in NYC.  The upstairs area might be okay, but the basement area needs to be shut down. It's a completely different ambiance from the main floor, sauces are haphazardly placed on some random carts without enough ladles and they didn't have enough spoons for diners??? Worst of all there was a hair AND a dead bug (looked like a baby cockroach) on the plates.  When we notified the waitress of this, there was no response or apology.  With all the great hot pot options in NYC, please skip and go somewhere else.
$37 Ayce great quality of meats and side dishes toppings - good value and service was very attentive as well

This was my first time ever doing hot pot and it was so fun!! We came at 4:30 on a Sunday and there was no wait, and the restaurant stayed fairly empty. It is a really cool restaurant with a wall of fire and it's fairly big and clean. The tables with the stovetops on them are so cool. Everyone looked like they were having a good time.

Our server was extremely attentive and helpful. I had never done hot pot before so I let my friend choose everything. The restaurant had so many options for broths, appetizers, meats, vegetables, anything you can imagine. Our server brought everything out super quickly. I tried so many new things which was awesome because it was all for one flat price. For about $40 each, plus tax and tip, we ate until our bellies were full, and then we were given pudding! Such a cool experience. I definitely want to come back here and try the skewers as well.

Customer service is bizarre and slightly rude/robotic. Food is mediocre with the seafood not tasting fresh at all. They serve you warm tap water, and don't care to fill your water either. 

Other things to mention. They complained about the tip that was given. If you do eat here take a shower when you get home unless you want to smell like hot pot. Plus they were racist towards us since they cleaned up a table next to us (they were Asian) and not us after eating. 

I don't recommend this place as it's over priced and simply not that good. Much better places to eat in the city for cheaper.
Great atmosphere! Highly recommend!Great place for a party!Fresh food and good service!

Pro tip: call ahead and they can put your name on the waitlist over the phone so you don't need to wait in person:-) I called in on Saturday night and only had to wait (from the comfort of my own home) for about an hour!! 

The service and value is pretty great here. Everyone was super nice, and the rounds of meat and other things we ordered came out very quickly. I tried the spicy broth, and it had great flavor. The meat quality was pretty good as well, very tender! I loved the variety and selection of vegetables and other topping you could put into the hotpot! There was honestly nothing I could think of that their menu was missing. They also give you a pudding and milk tea dessert that's soo refreshing after the hot soup!

There's a basement as well with ~7 tables. The main level is definitely more decorated, but I didn't mind sitting downstairs at all. I will definitely be back, especially since it's getting colder now and hot pot just hits the spot.

Best hot pot i ever had even though I've only ever tried three places total. Hot pot is slowly creeping into my top 3 places to eat of all time and LaoJie is to blame for my new obsession. Actually Han in Hartford ct did it for me and then LaoJie took it to the next level. This is a no frills place, cute atmosphere with the fires going, but very straight forward.
You step inside, wait a bit then once your sat you get right to it. The price is extremely reasonable. They have more choices of broths then the other places I've been to with much more depth of flavor. I always get the mind numbing my spicy broth and then continue to make a mind numbingly spicy dipping sauce. The fried pork that comes with the ayce is amazing in a yummy dipping sauce or alone as my daughter had it. I had the crab which was hard to eat, fatty beef, fatty pork, a delicious Chinese vegetable I can't remember the name of, allll the mushrooms, clams, lotus root (you have to cook them sooo long). Everything was so fresh. If I'm ever in the city and craving hot pot I will be returning. I'm sure there's other yummy hot pot places here, but the price, service, no frills atmosphere and delicious quality ingredients can't be beat I'm sure.

Was a group of 6, didn't have reservations but there was a table open for us when we arrived at 5pm. Would recommend reservations! Lots of great options. Meat was delicious and fresh. We enjoyed the milk tea pudding dessert. There is 5% the check if you pay all in cash. Will definitely come again!

Came here to warm up a freezing cold day and was extremely glad we did. Let me firstly say that I was just blown away by how good the service was! From getting help ordering, to automatic refills, to ninja-esque cleanup, it felt like there was always someone ready to help without feeling like you're being watched. 

As for the food, I've always had mixed feelings about the likes of hot pot and shabu, but my meal today has turned me into a believer again. We got half Mala and half herbal broth, and a mountain of meats, veggies, and skewers. Insane to me still that our entire meal was right around $100. I felt like a king! Meat quality was decent; I'm not expecting exquisite cuts of meat for an all you can eat, but I honestly was impressed by how good it was. 

The skewers were solid too, some better than others. I had one beef skewer that was perfectly cooked, and one beef skewer that was a bit dry. Our favorite one was the pork belly wrapped enoki! 

For the "cons" of our meal: the ambiance is a little strange and I couldn't really figure out what the theme was, particularly with the old tv's on the walls, but I'm guessing it's just retro themed? Honestly though, didn't care! The other thing is the sauce bar was just weirdly organized and we saw a dirty bowl mixed in with the clean ones. Lastly, I wanted a small bowl but everything besides the sauce dishes were plates, which is a little strange considering everything is dripping in broth, but it wasn't a huge deal. 

All in all, screaming deal for delicious all you can eat hot pot and skewers! If you're not particular about small details, I don't think there's anything to complain about here. I'll absolutely be back soon; it's looking like it'll be a cold winter!

Good value for AYCE hot pot (and bbq if you'd like), and probably the best hot pot in Chinatown! You can make a reservation by calling and there's a limit to your seating time. Food is solid and comes quick - great service too!

The ambiance was amazing, the hot pot broth was good, i got the spicy one. Service was nice and effcient, took like 5 minute for the food to come out. The house special sauce was refreshing as well. Final ending, 8.6/10 would come again

There aren't many hotpot places with individual pots. So, since my friends and I like different things in our pots, we wanted our own. I got the pork bone broth as my soup base, and it was good. If I ever go again, I would choose something else like the spicy broth. 

I wasn't too pleased with the choices of items for the hotpot, but since it's ayce. The one thing that I liked was how they came around and collected your coats or whatever you would like to put inside a clear bag under your table. It helps your clothes stay clean and not smell like food. I may come back again in the near future when I'm in the area.

A very authentic hot pot place and they have lots of different food options. You can choose combine BBQ and hot pot. The BBQ is pretty good too! The ambiance is nice too, I like the decoration inside. They also have good service, the staff are nice and they serve food very fast!

Great all you can eat hot pot in the city! I liked that we got individual soups because I like spicy and others in the group could not handle the heat.  The items were pretty standard for a hot pot restaurant, but what I liked instead of the usual ice cream at the end was the milk tea pudding.  It wasn't too sweet and was a nice ending to the meal.  Will be back soon!

So we visited this place as we were randomly enjoying the sites around soho and chinatown which we decided to walk in and grab a table, now this was new years week so expected to see a bunch of places packed during the holidays to the wait wasn't bad and had to wait 35 mins abucheos was great. We were seated and got to order right away. I have photos of the food and it was pretty good only downside we'd say was that we couldn't split a bill or ask to have 2 different types of food for example if a friend wanted hot pot and we would want the bbq portion they wouldn't allow it. But hey not the worse thing to happen but just insight for those who would have wanted something else on the menu. Over all price fairly and the food was good. Now onto the photos.

The management here sucks. Reserved a group of 14 and made us sit in 2 tables that could only fit 12people.
