Asked the front desk for help, and just like the other comments said, those girls acted like they don't care and rolled their eyes. So the two of us ended up only getting bbq and no hotpot. The hot pot was not bad, the bbq wasn't that good tho. If you have never tried Dolar Shop, the one in Flushing has AYCE, or Xiang Hot Pot Brooklyn(AYCE), or ChongQing Wharf Hot Pot(also AYCE), they all have more selection on meats and seafoods and desserts!

Bang for buck, this is probably one of the best values you'll find for hot pot in Manhattan. It's $35pp before tax/tip for AYCE hot pot, and you can either use a communal pot or individual pots. 

The veggies are super fresh and clean, the seafood is generous, and the meat is good quality. You can even order hot appetizers as part of the AYCE menu--the meat strips (fried pork) are surprisingly delicious, and we ended up getting several rounds of them. Throw in the quirky yet modern and elegant decor, and quick service, and you've at least justified making your hair and clothes stink.

Girl at the front (hostess?) was extremely rude. I said the time wrong at first and she just rolls her eyes at me. Felt like I was begging her to let us eat there. I did make a reservation. The food was just meh. I got the herbal chicken soup base which was extremely forgettable. 
Took my friends to try this out for my birthday but won't be coming back here.

Came on a Saturday with a group of 11 (best to make a reservation) for AYCE.

The ambience is nice, clean and spacious. Highly advise you to put your jackets in the bags so make sure your clothing doesn't soak in the smell. My personal favorites were their pork bone broth, fish filet, fried tofu skin, tripe, watercress, and milk tea flavored pudding and fried montau with condensed milk for dessert.

I deducted a point for service because one of our friends had broth likely spilled on his jacket by waiters as they were cleaning up - didn't admit to it which is irresponsible! Our friend didn't realize until we left. I'd be on the lookout for this.

One problem I had was that we had to share the hotpot for 2 couples because they placed our party of 14 into 2 tables that fits  only 12 people.   And they were sharing a small pot!  They should have just added a third table to accomodate the customers.   Or just offer discount on sharing pots!!

Make sure you let them know ahead of time that you don't want to share if you have a big party.  Or ask for discount!

My favorite hotpot place in Manhattan! Fair warning, the wait can get pretty long during peak hours/weekend but they are nice enough to let you call ahead and put your name down before your party arrives. It is AYCE for hotpot only or AYCE hotpot and skewers which also includes appetizers and dessert! The bone broth is my favorite one to get and their sauce station is well stocked and clean. The service is very fast and efficient as well. Key things to not skip out on are the chicken wings and dessert at the end! It is a refreshing milk tea with pudding and is a nice way to top off your meal. 10/10 would recommend everyone to go here for your hotpot cravings in the winter.

pretty good deal for an AYCE in Manhattan. Took a group of 7 and it was about 37$ each. we were able to take advantage of the birthday deal tho which was nice. the food that they bring out for the birthday deal was super fun too. all the food that they brought out was good. their sauce station also had a pretty good selection too.

I came here with a group of 10 on a Sunday night (called in a reservation the week prior). They gave our group a private room (2 tables) in the back of the restaurant. Servers were frequently attending our party - bringing in orders, refilling our drink pitchers, and ready for us to order more! It did feel a little rushed but being a younger crowd, we didn't have an issue with it. They suggested that we get large shareable pots with dividers rather than individual pots since we had 5 people per table. The menu has a large variety of items to order part of their AYCE hot pot. Quality of the food was alright, better than expected for AYCE. Priced pretty average compared to other AYCE hot pot restaurants. I would recommend coming with a younger crowd since it does seem fast paced and has loud music playing throughout the restaurant.

I was thoroughly impressed with LaoJie, a restaurant that made my first hot pot experience quite memorable. The expansive menu is very well priced, with generous portions and a DIY sauce bar. At a set price, you get to order unlimited items for either hot pot or barbecue, and can also combine the two. The service was well-paced and thoughtful-- for instance, they package your coats in a sealed bag to prevent the aromatic atmosphere from getting imbibed in the fabrics. The dipping broths were sumptuous and satisfying. The servers will patiently guide you through the process, especially if you are a novice to hot pot. The meal also included a complimentary dessert. At the end of the hour-long gastronomic extravaganza, be prepared to walk out feeling stuffed to the gills but with a beatific smile on your face.

Was visiting New York and I told my friend I wanted to get hotpot and this was one of her suggestions. 

Honestly, I don't think I'm super picky with hotpot - especially AYCE. As long as I feel like I'm about to burst out of my pants at the end of the meal, I consider it mission accomplished. Something I do appreciate from hotpot places is when they have quail eggs (one of my fave things to get) and they do!! 

Something that really stands out about this place, though, is the dessert at the end. Not 100% positive what it was, but it seemed like milk tea with egg pudding served in a bowl, and that is what makes this place stand out to me. I've never been to a hotpot place that serves you dessert at the end (excluding places that offer fruit and small desserts that you can get on your own). The dessert was so yummy and refreshing after a heavy hotpot meal. Even though I was full af at the end, I would've gladly taken a second serving of dessert.

I went on a Sunday around noon and was seated right away.  Service was great and wait staff super attentive.  They constantly came around to  replenish our broth and checked to see if we would like to order more food.  Out of all the hotpot places in Chinatown, this is to date my favorite.  I never felt rushed or pressured to finish quickly.   Food was good but I would skip the fried foods and just stick to the basics.  I definitely recommend ordering their soju.   It was cold and delicious!   Music was great as well and really catered to the younger crowd.  I would definitely go back.

This is my new fave hot pot spot in Manhattan. The price for AYCE is reasonable for the city (~$40 after tax/tip) and the food is high quality. Service was super fast as well. We called to make a reservation the night before for 2 and there were no issues. The broths and sauces are super fragrant. Overall had a really positive experience and can't wait to come back!!

Currently our go-to AYCE hot pot place! Seating is quick with a reservation as long as you have your full party, solid sauce options, and tons of hot pot dishes to order. 

We typically get individual pots, but you have the option of sharing a large one as well with two separate soup bases. I appreciate that each dish of ingredients is large enough so you don't have to order a ton of the same dishes (aside from meat of course!) and servers circulate frequently to clear empty dishes and take additional orders.

Haven't tried the skewer/BBQ option here.
Solid hotpot place. LaoJie is all you can eat. Love the shrimp paste and the dessert soup. Large selection of meats, seafood, and veggies.

This is my first time in the Manhattan location but I decided to check out this location because they have a skewer option and I love skewers. We came on a weekend afternoon and didn't wait for a table, but if you're coming for dinner I'd recommend having a reservation because there were a lot of people waiting by the time we left. 

The service here is quick and attentive! All the food we ordered came quickly, including the skewers which was nice because we were hungry. The restaurant is large and we were seating in a back room that had two tables which was quiet. This place has everything you need for hotpot - sauce, quick service, and servers whenever you need one, they were really good about keeping our soup and water refilled which is nice we never had to track anyone down. 

The meats and skewers were great but my favorite part is always the pudding dessert they have - super yummy way to finish off any meal

Went to capitalize on the free birthday meal offer. Expected fresh BBQ skewers but they were pre-grilled and just served. A bit of a letdown. However, the hotpot looked promising, even though I didn't give it a try. Maybe next time.

Honestly my favorite AYCE hotpot spot!! They have one in bk too and this one is conveniently in Chinatown. It's like $35 pp for hotpot but they also offer skewers too for extra. There are a bunch of items on their menu and everything is so good! I'm always rolling myself out! Interior is very old school and there's a flame design thing in the middle of the restaurant that's pretty cool! Large tvs and music playing and it's overall a good spot for good quality food items! And the best part is they end it with this super yummy pudding that's like mango and has some milk with it! They're also very fast with putting your order in and bringing the food out!

Good service. Went at lunchtime. Was pretty empty at this time of day. I wish they have a lunchtime pricing as time is limited during the lunch hour. 

Other than that we enjoyed the place.

Had a great experience at LaoJie. A little bit of a wait on a Saturday night but once we got seated service was quick and all of the food tasted great. We liked that they had french fries available which was fun. All food came as ordered and we also liked the individual hotpot style so everyone could pick their own broth.

Laojie continues to be my fave hot pot place in Chinatown! The service is always great esp for an AYCE place. The meats and other items are always brought super quickly when asked and they waiters refilled my soup at least 3 times during my meal. Also, their mango pudding tea dessert soup is so light and refreshing. Even though I was stuffed, I ate a whole bowl :)

They are able to do larger parties and accommodated 14 people for my friends bday.

Make sure u make rsvp! Came here with the gf and she enjoyed it! Everything was fresh and service was great! I've been to their bk locations so it was nice to finally goto their chinatown location. One of the best hotpot places in my book!
Really solid hotpot! My favorite were the beef and lamb. The service was pretty quick and we only got the hotpot but have heard the skewers are good.

Went to this place after a late night event. We were really glad that they took us in late. 

They had a big selection of food, some american, some dimsum, and a lot of meats. They also had a sauce bar where you can make your own dipping sauce for the food which is my favorite part about this place. They came out with the food QUICK and we got straight to cooking

It was a great experience especially since we ordered much more than what we could eat haha.

Will definitely go back to this place again if im around chinatown

Great service, great food and at a great price! Got the skewer hotpot combo for ~$43. 

They have plenty of options across the board, meat, veggies and seafood! Plus they have a free pudding dessert at the end of the meal that really tops it all off.

Didn't have a reservation was guided downstairs - 

We did the skewers + hotpot for $50 pp about and for hotpot you get to choose up to 3 broths 

The broth were basic - we got the herbal and bone .. but wish they had like a Tom yum or something

Skewers - I was expecting the seasoned ones you get in the street vendors but it was nottt , they tasted meh , lack of flavor and we only ended up getting one round (beef, squid, chicken wings, quail egg (that's different from most places it was good! And we love the corn cheese lol)
- the mussels were NOT good - I was scared to eat them , it was so rubbery I couldn't 

Hot pot: the quality of the meat was okay - they had lots of veggie options but we got tired of the flavors quick 
- love the fried tofu skin! 
- the sauces kind of fell short - they had all the basics but the peanut sauce didn't have much flavor 


Overall service was good - she was attentive and made sure we had time to put more orders in 

Service: every round we ordered, one of our items didn't come out , but at the end of the day it was fine cause we were getting full!

This restaurant has become the go-to for birthdays among many of my friends now due to their deal where the base fare is waived for the birthday person when going with 3 other paying customers.  Both times I've been we added the AYCE skewers as well for an additional $5 per person; I really like this added variety since sometimes I think with just AYCE hotpot it can feel a bit monotonous by the end of the meal.  The skewers are quite tasty, although I'd only recommend them if you're a fan of cumin. Overall, the ingredients taste fresh and high quality compared to many other AYCE places I've been. Service is quite attentive and helpful. One time we went and one person's individual stove wasn't working so they quickly resolved this by giving that person a large, 3-flavor pot instead which could go on the middle burner; the only downside to this was slightly less table space, but we were able to work around this by ordering smaller batches at a time. The ambiance is also great as there are cute booths and nostalgic Chinese decor.

Fantastic all you can eat hotpot plus BBQ for a little extra, with a great ambiance that's perfect for a date night or meet up with friends. Service is very fast and efficient - we never waited long for drinks or more food. They were very attentive, always checking on us... they deserve 5 stars alone. Call for reservations if coming for dinner or weekend lunch. 

We ordered one spicy and one non-spicy broth. Both were excellent, in particular the spicy one which wasn't so spicy that it overpowered the flavors. The menu was robust with the different meats and produce offered. We've learned to take it easy and not order too much in the beginning, and here it paid it because all the portion sizes were decent and not too much, so even if you don't like something THAT much you can still be confident to finish it. 

We opted to include the BBQ skewers. They were delicious but just know these are deep friend and not grilled, so any of you clean protein hitters might want to forgo them. 

Overall fantastic restaurant with fantastic service and excellent food.

Call for reservations!

LaoJie Hotpot serves three types of AYCE: hotpot, skewers, or hotpot and skewers. They offer a lot of selection for hotpot so our group of 3 all decided to go with AYCE hotpot ($36.98), as it would be more than enough to keep us filled without dipping into the skewers. 

And it was more than enough variety to keep our taste buds happy and tummies full! We enjoyed the fatty beef, beef tongue, pork belly, handmade fish paste, handmade shrimp paste, crab meat stick, and veggies. We each get our own hot pot, so I chose the mushroom soup base. Friend got the spicy beef tallow soup base, which does more than deliver a kick, so keep that in mind if you order it!

We were too full to try anything off the appetizer menu. Our meal ended with a complimentary dessert of mango milk tea pudding, which was light and refreshing.

Service was on top of things. Our requested items came out timely and our waters refilled. Space inside seems to support groups big and small.

Overall experience: 2 stars (this location specifically)
This ambiance and atmosphere is great, service is friendly and staff comes around to check up on you a good amount. However, I highly question their sanitary issues and freshness of food. I came when they first opened and everything seemed to be great, but I did have a stomachache after (I usually tend to anyway so I didn't think much). However, I waited a few months and came back, this time, I found a piece of hair on my plate when I first sat down. I notified the staff and they changed my plate. This is quite common in restaurants, however, during the same meal, we found another hair that looked like an eyelash or eyebrow hair in another dish of ours. In the middle of my meal, my stomach starts to hurt super bad and I could not eat another bite. This has never ever happened to me, ever, in any restaurant ever. Ever since this experience, I have never came back to this Laojie, but I have been back to the 8ave location a few times and never had a problem there. I highly suggest take the extra trip to 8ave for Laojie. I really wish their management would look into this problem and fix this because this is not ok.

Came here together with my two friends on a Wednesday night. The line is pretty short comparing with weekends. We waited less than 25 mins before get seated. 

This time I tried the pork belly, pig lung, and pig lever. Ah, not a big fan of pig lever/ lung. I still recommend you try the regular meat only. 

Pan fried dough is a must to order with condensed milk. Delicious!

I would say get both skewers and hotpot when you are here, it just completes the experience and makes this place different than the other ayce hotpot w/ bbq places. They have a great variety with their hotpot and skewers menu. The skewers were large in portion but do take a while to come so as you wait you can order from the hotpot menu. Their beef skewers did not have chucks of fatty parts which allowed me to enjoy them without having to chew through and get rid of the fat. I liked that this place has fish roe fish balls for hot pot, I know other places charge extra to get this. They end their experience with milk tea pudding which was sweet and satisfies the need for bubble tea afterwards. I left feeling very full. Service was quick and you get 5% off if you pay with cash. The only thing was some of the water they served was lukewarm and I had to ask for a cup of ice.

The staff was really friendly. Even though we had made a reservation, we still had to wait about 20 minutes so they gave us a free pitcher of a drink of our choice. We were there on a Thursday night so I imagine the weekend is even more hectic. You can go there for your birthday for free if you bring at least three other people with you, which is what we did. The food was pretty good! Lots of options for the hotpot and their mango pudding dessert was delicious, the perfect ending to the meal.

We came on a Saturday around 6 and was seated immediately! I recommend sitting on the main floor if possible since the basement was not the same vibe. 

We got the hotpot and skewer combo which was a great decision. The hotpot had an expansive menu while the skewers were more limited. Starting off with the hotpot, our favorites were the fatty beef, duck feet, and tripe. The lamb skewers were the best - tender and chewy. The beef on the other hand is too hard. 

The service was phenomenal - our waitress was very attentive, refilled and cleaned out table super quickly which made our experience much better

Best AYCE hot pot in nyc! The skewers are such a great addition (especially cumin lamb) and the quality is solid. The interior is fun, bustling, and inviting. Love this spot, love the location. Service is always good

Another solid hotpot & bbq place! Specifically, we were especially impressed by the skewers - very tender and well seasoned. The hotpot was also delicious, and all in all it's a relatively good value as an AYCE option. Also the restaurant itself was really interesting. While there elements of a traditional Chinese restaurant (a la Xiang Hot Pot), there are some fun quirky elements like the video game by the waiting area or the random TVs on the wall. It was a fantastic dinner experience, and we would definitely come back again for the skewers alone!

I have been to Laojie more than 5 times already. The vibe is very cozy and comfortable here. Staff is friendly and welcoming. A wide variety selection of food options to choose. My favorite broth is the tomato broth. It's very fresh. 
Knock out one star because the price has increased from $27.99 to 37? I believe. But again, this worth the value.

Tried the Chinatown location for the first time tonight for dinner. There was no wait- there's upstair seating and downstairs seating. Got half spicy and half bone broth. Soup base not bad for a AYCE place. Love that they have options like the mini buns with condensed milk, crispy pork and so on. The seafood here is surprising pretty fresh- crab,fish, shrimp paste and clams were all good. Service was great- everything came out so fast.

I'm a Hotpot lover & as we all know, not all hotpot restaurants are created equal. So here are the deets on this place:
- The most important for late night peeps: They say they're open til 12am on every posting. But we walked in at 10:45 and they said we could sit if we wanted to but the kitchen closes at 11 so we would have to order everything up front and not get any refills. Why post that you close at 12 when you close at 11? Anyway, we sat and ordered everything up front - like they asked - and they forgot to bring us our white rice. When I asked for it once I realized it was missing, our waiter told us it was too late and the kitchen had closed. This is also when they let us know (at 11:10pm) that the sauce bar was also closing so we had to get anything we wanted right now. I was pretty frustrated with that whole situation. But you know how it is when you're craving Hotpot - only Hotpot is the cure. 
- It is AYCE (can't remember the price but like normal $35-$40 range). 
- The food came very quickly and they were good about giving broth refills. 
- This place is very much a chill atmosphere. They were playing music pretty loudly. We enjoyed it but just an FYI for those who wouldn't.

For a restaurant that closes at midnight, they allowed my business partner and I in a half hour before they closed for a full meal and we never felt rushed. The food was delicious and the variety was unbeatable! Highly recommend!

Good hotpot! Very clean and affordable! Will definitely just go here than anywhere else!

Location: It is located in Chinatown. The interior is not that big, so I think its better if you make reservations! Street parking only!

Service: they are super nice and attentive! They quick to give you your order!

Food: Everything was delicious! The variety of meats, fishballs, rice cakes, sausages, veggies are good! The only thing that I don't like is their sauces! Not that much to choose from. At the end they gave you this jasmine jelly that is really really good!

Price rating: 6/10, it was not bad for food that you will get.

Definitely will come back here cause its worth the money! Everything was delicious!
Great menu selection and lots of sauces to create a wonderful meal. Just have fun trying out things. We tried assortment of meats, seafood n veg

This new AYCE hot pot place is so good! I love that they have booth seating (very comfortable) and feels clean which makes it kid friendly. We have been here a few times and have done the BBQ too but I personally just have always liked hot pot more than BBQ. 

You can get individual pots which I prefer over a big pot that you have to share. 

Food is great and everything came out fast. I love the mushroom broth too!

Service was great, everyone was on top of us and so nice to our kid.

Great for large groups of friends too. There is a two hour limit and a 5% cash discount so bring cash and ask for that!

Best hotpot in Chinatown. Soup base is very flavorful and all dishes/toppings are included in the all you can eat, including seafood and appetizers. Service was great and fast and waiters/waitress are friendly and professional. Great ambience, the fake fire is cute.

Always love a good AYCE hot pot and IN MANHATTAN this place is a steal at $35. So many options, fresh meats and they also do AYCE appetizers which is the first time I've seen it. It does get busy so definitely make a res or go on a weekday, but it is worth if you eat your fill!!!

I made reservations over a phone call. This is an all-you-can-eat place within a fixed time frame (I think it was 2 hours). We were seated promptly on time. 

There were plenty of soup options and you can select up to two options. We also picked the hotpot with BBQ option which was definitely worth it. 

Food portions were great and the quality was great. I loved almost every BBQ skewer I ordered. The quality of the hotpot meats and veggies were good too. Everything looked fresh. 

Would definitely recommend LaoJie especially if you're looking for a hearty meal with friends. 

Also, don't forget to ask for a discount if you pay by cash!
Food is fresh and a lot of choices to choose from. Server are just a bit forget full . Ambiance is good we had the back room and it was cozy and less noisy.

i love laojie!! the meat quality is pretty good and their menu is very expansive. they give you the food pretty quick but it is sometimes hard to track the workers down. they're very attentive though. i love the ambiance and the interior of the restaurant!! the cool fire in the middle haha it's also really great for big parties! we had a party of 12 at 9:00 PM and they seated us no problem!

I love love LOVE this place. This is my absolute favorite place to get hotpot in manhattan. This place is great in all aspects. Just the service itself is worth coming here for. They have so many servers who are all very active in taking orders and attending your table. When I eat here, there almost never a moment when there isn't food on my table unlike some other AYCE places. The pricing is also very reasonable, and for an extra couple bucks you can also get the AYCE skewers, though I've only been for the hotpot. 

In terms of the food, they have a pretty large selection with most things that I like to have for hotpot. They're also one of the few places I've been that let you do three different soups so you can try everything out. My favorite broth is their bone broth but the tomato broth is also good. 

This location is fantastic and even the restaurant itself just has really cool vibes with the decor of the flames.

One of the best AYCE hotpot restaurant in the Manhattan area, and their waiters and waitresses reacts very fast and nicely to my demand. The food is ok, although it is not that totally Sichuan spicy, but still fresh and good.

I really enjoyed this hot pot place. The ingredients all were fresh and plenty of good ingredients as well. Also for quality and all you can eat I felt like this was a good price. Would certainly come back again for the hotpot. Service was very attentive as well. The place was clean overall and really enjoyed my experience.

Friendly staff, good selection of soup bases, items, and good ambiance but it can get super loud especially with so many birthdays. If it's your birthday, bring your ID and at least 3 people with you (total 4 people) because you (the birthday person) can dine for free and a birthday song will be played for you. They offer hotpot, BBQ skewers or an option to do both.

This location could get really packed so I recommend making a reservation in advance to avoid the 1-2 hour wait. Make sure your party is all there before being seated because they do implement a 2 hour dining time limit. 

Overall the food quality was good when I went. Definitely try their fried buns with condense milk appetizer and they give you a delicious milk tea pudding dessert at the end!

Big fan of LaoJie. I was super excited to see they opened a Manhattan location. Fresh ingredients and a good selection of AYCE dishes. The staff is super friendly and attentive. The ambiance of the restaurant is dark and cozy.

Very cool decor, it's on ! Except it's actually smoke under red lights so no one gets burned. Pretty interesting selection of cooked items. I'd probably not order too much fried food, but the chicken wings were pretty good. They had McDonald's style French fries, which someone at my table ordered. Definitely a trap. 
There's an extensive list of sauces you can make, even with straight up sugar to put into your soy sauce. In terms of meat options, it's nothing fancy. No a,b,c tiers of wagyu beef or whatever, but they do have an option for skewers I might try next time. I probably got mussels and beef the most. Beef tongue is great. The pork we got was kind of strange since it was 99% fat and no meat. I came on my birthday so I was free, and my 3 other friends got a slight discount too. They even play a birthday remix song and light a candle on top of a fried dough bun.

I went with a table for 4 including me on a Wednesday evening at 7pm. It's best to call ahead to reserve a table. I called the day before to prevent any long wait times. 

When upon seated we were given a chance for a raffle per table. We got the surf clams for free from the scratch off card. We didn't know that we couldn't get the 5% off discount when pay by cash if we participate on the scratch off card raffle. It was confusing since they said promotions couldn't be combined...?? It's doesn't make sense if paying with cash is considered as a "promotion" in order to get the 5% off. So we explained we'd rather opt for paying with credit card. But we pay by cash anyway without the discount because we had someone in our table birthday that was within 3 days. 

Anyway, let me talk about the food and service. I went to the Brooklyn one a few times and was surprised it expand to Chinatown so this was my first time at the Chinatown location. Food wise, it's more options including lots of seafoods like crabs, clams, etc. the quality food seems a little higher to other hotpot places. As for the service, the employees with check on the table to refill the broth, skimp away the scum from the broth, and remove empty plates. At the end of paying the bill, they will include a complimentary mango milk tea pudding dessert which is my favorite.

I got two different soup bases, but you can get up to three!

This was a fun lunch experience for me.  When you enter, they have like fire going up in the middle of the restaurant, but it's not real flames. We got a booth table, so the seats were wooden hard. The soup pot itself was double the size of my head. 

They served veggies in wicker baskets. All the skewers came on one plate. The meats didn't look frozen. 

The condiment and sauce bar is closer to the front entrance. Their house special sauce is actually numbing spicy!  Also, they offered to give us the spicy dipping seasoning/powder. That was great too. I love that shhh. 

Before we left, the server reminded us that they have dessert. It was milk tea with pudding!!! IT WAS SO GOOD. 

There were a couple times when our server would scoop out the meat gunk from our hot pot. That was the first time I had a server do that for me at an AYCE hot pot joint. I was pleasantly surprised. 

The restrooms are in the back. They accept credit card payment, but you get 5% discount if paying cash.

Came here for hotpot the other night (my second time here), and left so full I almost threw up (gluttonous, I know). We came on a Saturday evening and put ourselves on the waitlist around 7PM, and waited ~1.5 hours total, so if you're planning to go, would definitely get ahead of it and either make a reservation or put yourself on the waitlist earlier. 

The cost per person pre-tax was $37 each, so you end up paying just under $50 per person in the end. In comparison to 99 Favor Taste which is $30 per person, I'd say you're largely paying for the ambiance and slightly more variety / higher quality. Lao Jie has a few additional seafood items that 99 Favor doesn't have such as clams and fish paste. 

The staff comes by quite frequently by your table to skim oil, put your shrimp paste in, refill on broth, or to take your order. They're also super fast with getting your order out to you - after ordering, food always comes out in 2 minutes or so. 

They also have a mango dessert at the end that's super refreshing and delicious. Much needed after the meal.

The dessert is so so so good! 

Soup base: recommend spicy pot. It's not that spicy and you can always ask for less spicy as needed.

Meat: my favorite meat options are lamp, and beef tone. 
Dessert: the fried sticky rice is must have. It surprises me when I take the first bite. 

Staff there is friendly and welcoming. They change the plate on time and keeps the table clean. 

It's quite noisy and busy. Definitely my fav place for hot pot.

Great food, service,  and ambiance.  Also this is the first place I have gone for hotpot so I don't have anything to compare it to. With that being said everything was delicious and tasted fresh. 


Make sure you come hungry

Excellent service and ambiance, extensive drink list, a private room for up to maybe 10, great bar for making custom dipping sauces, lots of delicious cooking broths and super fresh food items, and you can opt for individual hotpots or a large one for the table. Perfect for large groups or a fun interactive food experience for a date.

My friends recommend me Laojie hotpot. So we decided to try it yesterday. Wait is about 1.5 hours during Saturday night. We walked around and finally our table is ready. 
Menu has well selected options. The self-serve sauce section has 10+ dipping sauce that you can do a diy mix. 

Soup base: recommend the herbal soup base cause I can't handle spicy. 

I like the sliced lamp and imitation crab meat stick. Vibe is good. Also saw people celebrate their birthday.

One of the better AYCE hotpot restaurants! We came on a Saturday evening and there was such a lively atmosphere. The place was packed and there were a bunch of people waiting to be seated but luckily we made reservations in advance. Not particularly amenable to larger groups since the biggest table can sit max 6 people but they were able to seat our group of 12 at two adjacent tables. Service was very friendly and attentive. We were provided bags to stash our belongings in to prevent them from catching the smell of the food. The hotpots were frequently refilled with water and we never had a problem flagging down a waiter whenever we needed something. 

On to the food! The sauce station was pretty standard. I loved their homemade sauce and enjoyed dipping all of my food in it. The tomato soup base was a good choice and flavored all of the food perfectly. All of the seafood and veggies tasted fresh. Surprisingly I was not a huge fan of the meats though because they were either too fatty or cut too thinly. If you're in a particularly carnivorous mood, I would recommend ordering twice the amount of meat that you typically order because they only come in a few thin slices per order. We also opted for unlimited BBQ skewers and they were all deliciously seasoned with cumin. Birthday cake + birthday song for diners celebrating their birthdays and milk tea pudding for dessert, perfect way to end the meal.

The only reason why they don't get 5 stars is because they mentioned that there was no corkage fee when we made our reservations but warned us that there would be one when we took out our drinks. Not cool and something to keep in mind if you're planning to byob.
This was my last meal before leaving NYC and was definitely my favorite meal! The restaurant was very clean! Service was great, very attentive and quick! I will definitely return when I am in town!

99 Favor but ~elevated~ in quality and in ambience! From the plastic bags offered to keep your coats fresh to the seafood options included at no additional cost, this is definitely my new fave AYCE hotpot in the city (2nd is 99 Favor, 3rd is Hou Yi, 4th is Hometown)

Hot pot ~$35 10/10
-peep those menu options, they've got all the key players and more
-either individual pots or 3 soup pot to share
-lamb over beef. the beef just withers away in the soup but the lamb has some substance to it
-i usually dont think the soup makes a difference but the spicy and tomato soup really seeps into the veggies/meats/noodles. and the beef tendon soup had one marrowy bone marrow yummmmm 
-notable mention: apps and seafood included!! no extra $$!! 

This takes the #1 spot of AYCE in Manhattan. Price is on point, a lil more than 99 Favor but cheaper than others, quality is there, and ambiance... fire appearing mist, screens showing music videos w lyrics, woodsy plantsy tranquil but lively spot. This would impress visitors especially, or Manhattan hotpot enthusiasts who are too lazy to train to Queens like me

I've been to their Brooklyn location so I was excited to find out they opened a location in Chinatown. Much closer to where I live. It's $34.95 pp for AYCE hot pot. They "accept" credit cards but it seems like that depends on the day. When we entered, the lady at the front as they were only doing cash that day. Didn't give a reason as to why but that was annoying. 

Anyways for the actual hotpot, there is a variety to meats, seafood and veggies to choose from as well as soup base options. Their house chili sauce is good, so I recommend trying that. Their pudding dessert is also good, you can get more than 1 bowl too.

came here with another friend who also had a birthday within 3 days of dining to take advantage of the free birthday meal deal (bring 4 paying diners and the birthday person eats for free). 

Food (4/5) - AYCE. Sauce bar pretty normal, nothing too extensive. Their house sauce is not too thick / thin, well flavoured if you're the lazy type. Food quality is fine. We particularly liked the assortment of meat / roe balls, tripe, various innards (pork kidney / liver), fish. Meat quality is decent, prefer the fattier types here. Soup base we liked both the spicy one (actually not too spicy, you have been warned) and the pork bone broth.

Appetizers are free - definitely try the pumpkin pancake. We even got extras at the end as dessert!

Provided dessert is mango pudding, it's more like mango jello in coconut / evaporated milk. Was yummy even if it's not what I expected as mango pudding.

Price (5/5) - low 30s / person, drinks not included except for water. Nothing to scoff at.

Service (5/5) - everything was pretty fast, and we didn't really have to ask twice. Staff were polite, efficient, knew what they were doing. Only complaint is that our group of 10 got split up into a table of 6 + 4.

Ambiance (5/5) - Rowdy! Not too loud. They provide plastic bags for your coats so that they don't get contaminated by the smell, which is a nice touch. Nice and bright, clean.

We had a great time. Come hungry, they don't rush you out. About $37 per person. We had three teenagers with us and got our money's work. Excellent staff!!!! And if it is your birthday be prepared for song. It is really loud.

a solid place for AYCE hot pot! 

the food: good variety and i enjoyed the fish roe balls the most, my only thing is that their sauce bar isn't my favorite compared to others and the beef quality is just okay. 

the space: big and our party even got to be seated in a more private room, giving us plenty of space and privacy. 

the service: everyone is really nice and attentive. it was my friends bday and the entire crew came to sing for her :)

Good for large groups not a lot of choices I feel like they used to
Have more food choices now it's not a lot and they rush you
